{{Alliance}} {{RaceIcon|Human|Female}} [[Moranna Rosenberg]] | fleader = | mount = | homeworld = [[Vorgendor]] | environment = | area = [[Ashenvale]], [[Silverpine Forest]], [[Duskwood]], [[Gilneas]] | language = Unknown | exact = | height = | weight = | organization = | alignment = | source = }} '''Worgen''' are large, wolf-like creatures that inhabit and hunt in darkened forests throughout the Eastern Kingdoms, such as Duskwood and Silverpine Forest. Nightmarish beings of legend, worgen originate from a world nestled far within the Dark Beyond, [[Vorgendor]], and much of their nature is shrouded in mystery. ==History== ===Early history=== Originally, the worgen were [[Elune]]'s favored children, created to serve as guardians against the encroaching darkness. Their blood was said to be as pure as the water of the night elves' moonwells and they were deeply connected to Elune. However, use of blood magic rose amongst their ranks in a desperate attempt to fend off the demonic forces of the Burning Legion that sought to consume their world, corrupting their noble heritage. Despite turning to the use of dark magic, the worgen have been fighting a losing battle against the lords of the Emerald Flame.[[Vorgendor: Myths from the Blood Dimension]] The masters of blood magic, pricoliches, rose to power and sealed away the [[Scythe of Elune]] to prevent it from falling into the wrong hands.{{Neutral}} [[File:Priest (Class Icon).png|16px]][[File:Mage (Class Icon).png|16px]][[File:Warlock (Class Icon).png|16px]][[File:Druid (Class Icon).png|16px]] [60] [[Wisdom of Ur]] During the reign of the Kaldorei Empire, Queen Azshara and the highborne delved into forbidden arts, opening portals to realms such as the worgen's home-world of Vorgendor.{{Neutral}} [[File:Priest (Class Icon).png|16px]][[File:Mage (Class Icon).png|16px]][[File:Warlock (Class Icon).png|16px]][[File:Druid (Class Icon).png|16px]] [60R] [[Scythe of the Goddess (6)]] ===Ur's research=== The wizard [[Ur]] of [[Dalaran (kingdom)|Dalaran]] studied the worgen sometime before the fall of Dalaran, ascertaining their existence beyond mere myth. Ur maintained that the worgen lived in a different world than Azeroth; a dark, brutal world of nightmare and shadow, where the lupine beings had full domain over the land. Concerningly, Ur discovered that the worgen could be summoned from this plane through dark rituals. He recorded his findings in two volumes of the eponymous "[[Book of Ur]]"[https://database.turtle-wow.org/?item=6283 The Book of Ur][https://database.turtle-wow.org/?item=61795 Book of Ur: Volume Two] and "[[Vorgendor: Myths from the Blood Dimension]]", the first volume of the former which would later fall into the possession of the mage [[Arugal]]{{Horde}} [26D] [https://database.turtle-wow.org/?quest=1013 The Book of Ur] and the second volume having been found in the libraries of [[Gilneas City]].{{Alliance}} [45D] [https://database.turtle-wow.org/?quest=41112 Ravencroft's Ambition] A copy of the second fell into the hands of [[Nefarian]], lord of Blackrock and head of the Black dragonflight, but had been damaged beyond use; a second copy of "Vorgendor: Myths from the Blood Dimension" was found within the expansive libraries of [[Medivh]], the Last Guardian of Tirisfal. Ur's research led to him personally delving into the realm of Vorgendor at the risk of both his life and sanity, beholding their heavens. He discovered that the worgen once held the Moon in reverence akin ao [[Night elf|elves of yore]], and that they spoke of a blue moon that once "danced across their skies". In Vorgendor, however, he saw not a tranquil blue, but a blood-red moon that cast a crimson pall over their world. Through fortune, he was able to communicate with one of their blood mages, who made him privy to a prophecy about the return of their Moon Goddess heralding their salvation. The prophecy foretold a day where the Blue Moon would return, opening a gateway to a new realm untouched by the Emerald Flame, where the worgen might thrive anew. ===The Third War=== During the Third War, Archmage Arugal summoned forth worgen in order to combat the onslaught of Scourge assailing Dalaran. Using the Book of Ur, Arugal succeeded in calling forth the worgen, and initially the plan was a resounding success. It soon became clear, however, that the beasts could not be controlled, and the worgen soon turned on their masters. Having been driven mad with guilt, Arugal retreated to [[Shadowfang Keep]], where he began to see the beasts he summoned as his children. The maddened wizard would go on to curse the inhabitants of nearby Pyrewood Village with enchanted shackles, whereby they would transform into worgen every nightfall.{{Alliance}} [27D] [https://database.turtle-wow.org/?quest=60108 Arugal's Folly]{{Horde}} [15] [https://database.turtle-wow.org/?quest=99 Arugal's Folly] Around this time, the kaldorei priestess Velinde Starsong was tasked with cleansing Felwood of the demons who dwelled there. Seeking a means to uproot the Burning Legion remnants without further night elf casualties, she prayed to Elune for an answer. Seemingly guided by the goddess, Velinde discovered an ancient artifact called the Scythe of Elune. With it, the priestess was able to tap into the dimension of the wolf-men and summoned them to Azeroth to combat the Legion. In truth, a pricolich had discovered the world of Azeroth and saw an opportunity to expand his influence, and the Scythe was gifted to Velinde through a grand deception in which she believed it was a gift from Elune herself. With the Scythe in hand, Velinde summoned the worgen to Azeroth - and initially, they fought valiantly against the demonic forces of the Burning Legion, their centuries of combat experience making them formidable allies. However, the pricoliches' influence over the worgen was absolute, turning their servants into mindless and obedient soldiers with no sense of self. Though initially concealed beneath layers of enchantments, the pricoliches began to reassert their dominion over their servants, culminating in the arrival of a pricolich in Azeroth. Velinde soon lost control of the pack and realized that the worgen were multiplying rapidly.[https://database.turtle-wow.org/?item=5520 Velinde's Journal] Desperately seeking a way to fix this, Velinde read many tomes from the libraries of Darnassus and even spoke to the Circle of Ancients themselves, who seemed to be unaware of the worgen's existence. Hearing rumors of Arugal's similar feats, Velinde traveled to the Eastern Kingdoms in hopes of consulting with the wizard, but perished in Duskwood before she could complete her mission. The Scythe was lost for a time before being re-discovered by Jitters, who accidentally summoned a pack of worgen to Duskwood. The worgen would go on to populate the haunted forest and harass the citizens of Darkshire.[https://database.turtle-wow.org/?item=2560 Jitters' Completed Journal] ===World of Warcraft=== With the return of the Blue Child in the skies of Azeroth, the prophecy as told to Ur of the coming of the worgen was heralded. Two pricoliches, [[Keeper Gnarlmoon]] and [[Father Lycan]], infiltrated Azeroth to advance their plans and open a portal to Vorgendor. Keeper Gnarlmoon was summoned to Azeroth by his minions and took refuge within the [[Tower of Karazhan]], whereas Father Lycan crossed the bridge to Azeroth in [[Silverpine Forest]] and then crawled over the [[Greymane Wall]] into the human nation of [[Gilneas (kingdom)|Gilneas]], which had fallen under the control of the black dragonspawn under the guise of the human nobles [[Celia Harlow|Celia]] and [[Mortimer Harlow]]. After they lost contact with [[Deathwing]], their regime as Regent-Lords of Gilneas had gone to a crawl until Father Lycan introduced himself to them in the middle of the night, offering them power and purpose in exchange for an alliance.[[Celia's Journal]] By the events of the [[Gilnean civil war]], the Bloodclaw and Nighthowl worgen packs had infested Gilneas through Oldrock Pass, and the Darkpelt pack led by [[Packmaster Ragetooth]] had even breached the capital city of [[Gilneas City]]. [[Moranna Rosenberg]], an erstwhile apprentice of Arugal, has since established [[Lupine Coven|a small cult]] in [[Hollow Web Cemetery]], where she and her followers have willingly infected themselves with the worgen curse in an attempt to "…seek power and healthiness beyond what the human body is capable of."{{Alliance}} [https://database.turtle-wow.org/?quest=40953 Vilest of Men] They had yet to test the curse on races other than humans and dwarves, but unlike Arugal they were not so depraved as to force it upon those unwilling.[[Moranna Rosenberg#Quotes]] ==References== {{reflist}} [[Category:Worgen]] [[Category:Races]]

'''William Voss''' was a renowned alchemist of [[Stormwind (kingdom)|Stormwind]] prior to the First War, operating out of his family's home in the city's [[Old Town]]. After the end of the Second War and the rebuilding of Stormwind, William assumed his house to be restored, given his importance as Stormwind's most renowned alchemist. However, the [[House of Nobles]]' plans for reconstructing the city did not include the rebuilding of the Voss family alchemy shop, leaving the Voss family homeless. Condemning those responsible for his family's fate, William sent his son [[Jared Voss|Jared]] to join the [[Stonemasons Guild|Stonemasons]] that shared his disdain for Stormwind's nobility before his death.<ref>{{questlong|Alliance|20D|Turning Off The Tap}}</ref>

WowLua is an in-game Lua scripting environment. It provides an interactive Lua interpreter, a multi-page script editor, syntax highlighting, and convenient commands for running scripts directly from chat or macros. == Installation == '''GitAddonsManager''' The easiest way to keep '''WowLua''' up to date is by using [[GitAddonsManager]]. # '''Add the Repository:''' Add the following URL to GitAddonsManager: https://github.com/laytya/WowLuaVanilla.git # '''Select the Branch:''' Ensure that the master branch is selected. # '''Update:''' Using GitAddonsManager, you can check for and install updates for all your AddOns with a single click. '''Manual Installation''' If you prefer manual installation, follow these steps: # Go to the main page of the repository. # Click the '''<> Code''' dropdown and download the repository as a .zip. # Unpack the .zip and rename the folder to WowLuaVanilla, removing the -master suffix. # Move the folder into your Interface/AddOns directory and restart the game. == Git Links == * [https://github.com/laytya/WowLuaVanilla '''(laytya)'''] == Commands == {| class="fandom-table" !Slash Command !Description !Usage Example |- |/lua or /wowlua |Opens the WowLua editor, optionally executes a Lua expression if provided |/lua print(14) |- |/luarun |Runs a specific script page by name or number |/luarun MyScript or /luarun 1 |- |/wowluarun |Alias for /luarun |/wowluarun MyScript or /wowluarun 1 |} == Bindings == Bindings (Hotkeys) * '''Toggle WowLua''': TOGGLE_WOWLUA — Show or hide the Lua editor window. * '''Run Page''': RUN_WOWLUA — Execute the current script. * '''Save Page''': SAVE_WOWLUA — Save the current script. * '''Create New Page''': Bind to create a new script page. * '''Navigate Pages''': Bind keys for previous/next page. == Preview == [[File:Wowlua.png|frameless|380x380px]] == Key Features == * '''Interactive Lua Interpreter''': Execute Lua code instantly. * '''Multi-Page Script Editor''': Save, rename, delete, and switch between multiple script pages. * '''Syntax Highlighting''': Color-coded code for easier readability. * '''Command Line Execution''': Run scripts via slash commands. * '''Global print()''': Redirects output to the WowLua output window when running code. * '''Bindings''': Hotkeys for toggling, running, saving, and managing scripts. [[Category:Addon]]

A fully functional Texas Holdem Poker mod. Play poker with your friends while waiting for spawns, raids, or looking for groups. == Installation == # Download this zip: [https://drive.google.com/file/d/1VgjvNZVOUhRnp3bO_6azilrE0DKKK1YC/view '''WoWTexasHoldem.zip'''] # Unzip the folder into your Interface\AddOns directory. == Starting a Game == * '''As Dealer:''' Type /holdem * '''Join a Game (as Player):''' Type /holdem PlayerName (replace PlayerName with the dealer's character name) '''Dealer Controls''' * To start dealing, right-click your player box or type /holdem as dealer. * To stop dealing, click the "Quit" button or run /holdem again as dealer. '''Joining or Watching a Table''' * Type /holdem PlayerName to join or spectate. == Playing the Game == * '''Deal Cards:''' As dealer, click "Play" or run /holdem to deal hole cards. * '''Betting:''' Use buttons: ** '''Fold:''' Click to fold your hand. ** '''Call:''' Match the current highest bet. ** '''Raise:''' Increase the bet by the set amount. ** '''All In:''' Bet all your chips. ** '''Adjust Raise:''' Use "+" or "-" buttons to change raise size. '''Sit Out / Back In''' * Click "Sit Out" to leave the hand temporarily. * Click "I'm Back" to rejoin. '''Ending a Game''' * As dealer, click "Quit" or type /holdem to stop the game. == Commands == {| class="fandom-table" !'''Command''' !'''Description''' !'''Usage''' |- |/holdem |Start a game as dealer or join a table |/holdem |- |/holdem PlayerName |Join or spectate a game hosted by PlayerName |/holdem PlayerName |- |/holdem 'PlayerName' |Same as above, explicitly specifying PlayerName |/holdem 'PlayerName' |- |(Right-click player box) |Start dealing / set dealer (via UI) |Right-click on your player box |} {| class="fandom-table" !'''Buttons in the UI''' !'''Description''' |- |'''Play''' |Deal hole cards / start the game |- |'''Quit''' |End the current game |- |'''Sit Out''' |Leave the hand temporarily |- |'''I'm Back''' |Rejoin the hand after sitting out |- |'''Fold''' |Fold your hand during play |- |'''Call''' |Match the current highest bet |- |'''Raise''' |Increase the bet by your set amount |- |'''Raise + / -''' |Adjust the raise amount (via "+" or "-" buttons) |- |'''All In''' |Bet all your chips |} * Minimize support: Click the minimap button to minimize/maximize. * Dealer can set chips, start dealing, or boot players via right-click menus. * Show your cards manually with "Show Cards" option during showdown. == Preview == [[File:WTH.png|frameless|380x380px]] == Version == Version Updates Summary '''v1.21''' * Minimize support via minimap button * Flash notification when it's your turn * Fixed crash bug related to showing cards after losing chips * Resizable window: 50%, 75%, 100% '''v1.20''' * Blink indicator for waiting players * Dealer button moves around * Sit out feature * 30-second timer for player actions * Fixed "All In" button display bug [[Category:Addon]]

{{Character|name="Wiley"|faction=Unknown|location=Stormwind, the King's Lands|occupation=Unknown|status=Alive|marital=Single|gender=Man|height=6'0"|weight=170 lb.|eyes=Brown|hair=Reddish-brown (copper)}}

'''"Wiley"''' is a human who was raised in [[Westfall]], Eastern Kingdoms. While the majority of his past isn't public knowledge, there are several records few and far in between detailing excerpts assumed to be of his life. 

Wiley was born in an unknown region in Year 596 of the King's Calendar, but as an infant was taken by his aunt to live a new life in Westfall, hopefully free from the claws of war that grasped the eastern territories of the King's Lands. His aunt raised him to be an upstanding member of society and even a soldier like her brother and his father, whom Wiley knew nothing about. Wiley's aunt had him taught at the Westfall Church before its shutdown, where until the age of 10, he followed a path relatively free of danger or any real risk to his life. 

But Wiley yearned for a life of action, and coupled with his aunt's degrading living situation in the countryside, he wanted to find another way to keep her and himself financially secure. Wiley and his best friend Aaron began to skip classes at the church, sneaking off with other mutual friends to mess around and loiter on the farmers' property and plots around the land. At the age of 12, Aaron confessed to Wiley that he joined the Defias Brotherhood -- which was still early in its creation -- and asked Wiley to join him. Wiley was unsure of a life of crime. He wanted to be rich one day to take care of his aunt, and hopefully find his father -- but the idea of breaking the law put fear in his heart. He declined, and Aaron's new Defias mentor ordered the recruits to make a lesson out of Wiley to show to Aaron what would happen if he ever defected. Wiley was called a noble sympathizer and left bruised and beaten nearly to death by the other kids, left missing for days. From that day on, Wiley never saw Aaron again.

Wiley was found by an older man by the name of Garec -- a retired Kul Tiran sailor, living in Westfall to retire with what little he had from his military days. Since Wiley had no one else in his life, Garec took it upon himself to raise the boy. Wiley felt betrayed by Aaron, and enraged at the Defias for ripping his friend away from his life, motivated to take the fight to them directly. While Garec disagreed and told Wiley that he was too young, he promised he would train him to fend for himself. 

While Wiley learned how to use standard-grade military weaponry by the young age of 14, he favored a bow and arrow, if not for its accuracy but its lack of danger and separation from ever getting nearly killed again. Wiley took up hunting to feed Garec as he grew older and unable to feed himself, returning the favor of being raised by doing good for his new father figure.

At the age of 15, Wiley enlisted in the King's Armies of Stormwind. While he was young, the kid showed promise, and his commanding officer noted that the boy had several qualities worth praise and recognition: 

''"Despite his childish antics within the barracks, Recruit [REDACTED] shows courage, bravery, and honor on the battlefield and in the line of duty. While he isn't as martially inclined as his fellow soldiers yet, the boy is exceptional with a bow and an arrow. We will watch his tenure with great curiosity."''

- Commanding Officer Breckensworth, of the Stormwind Army (Year 611 of the King's Calendar)

==== Present Day (Since 25 ADP/617 KC) ====
It wasn't long before Wiley was recommended by his CO to become a Private at age 17, and then a Squire at Age 19, before achieving Knighthood status at the young age of 22, by the year 618 of the King's Calendar. 

For the next section, it is almost entirely unknown (ICly, as well as OOCly) where Wiley's whereabouts have been up until recent -- for the past five years, he has not been seen, spotted, or recognized in public. 

Wiley served as a Knight of Stormwind's armies for three years, before being dishonorably discharged under command of his Knight Captain: 

''"Knight [REDACTED] has breached the sworn oath of knighthood by violating the trust, honor, and respect of His Majesty and His Armies. He is indefinitely, indisputably, dishonorably discharged as of 621 K.C."'' 

- Knight-Captain Dalonath, of the Stormwind Army (Year 621 King's Calendar)

Without any proper jobs or offers for consistent pay, Wiley begrudgingly turned to a life of crime, eventually learning to enjoy it as the only way he could remember his childhood best friend by, and without any other true option given his legal predicament.

[[Image:Windshear_crag.jpg|thumb|Windshear Crag]]
'''Windshear Crag''' once was a massive old-growth forest nestled in a valley in the [[Stonetalon Mountains]]. This cut in the mountains leads from the southern border of Ashenvale into the stormy canyons of the Stonetalons.

The Crag is now home to a massive logging expedition by the [[Venture Company]]. The once green landscape is now a barren area of tree stumps, polluted waters, and creaking machinery. The entire logging operation was put in the hands of [[Gerenzo Wrenchwhistle]], a gnome who is now more machine than gnome. Using his mechanical expertise, he built the [[Super Reaper 6000]] which can reduce the most massive trees to sawdust. He watches over the crag from a platform built above the [[Cragpool Lake]].

In the southeast corner of Windshear Crag lies the [[Windshear Mine]]. Kobolds occupy the mine and are digging for [[Smoky Iron Ingot]]s. In the northeast corner is the [[Talondeep Path]]. This cave stretches under the mountains and exits in [[Ashenvale]]. Nearby the entrance is [[Braug Dimspirit]], a [[Tauren]] that administers the Test of Lore to members of the [[Horde]].

[[image:wolf.png|right|/chomp]]
A carnivorous, furry, [[canine]] [[beast]] that often runs in packs. Wolves are known to be unable to [[Swim|swim]] (at least in [[World of Warcraft]]).  Wolves encountered in the wilderness are typically [[hostile]] and [[aggro|attack]] characters that approach them too [[Aggro_Radius|closely]].

Wolves are indigenous to many parts of Azeroth. The live in [[Elwynn Forest]], the [[Hinterlands]], [[Mulgore]], [[Duskwood]], [[Silverpine Forest]], the [[Badlands]], [[Tirisfal Glades]], [[Dun Morogh]], [[Felwood]], [[Burning Steppes]], [[Ashenvale]], [[Feralas]], the [[Western Plaguelands]], [[Blackrock Spire]], and [[Shadowfang Keep]].  They have a wide variety of sub-species and social habits. Though
most wolves are [[hostile]] towards humans and demi-humans who encroach upon their territories, a few unique dire wolf packs have befriended the Horde in recent years. There is a larger variety of wolf called [[Worg]]s; these are used as the [[orc]] [[mount]]. [[Orc]] [[shamans]] seem to hold them in high regard evidenced by the fact that their armor often has a wolf on them.

=== Game Value ===
* At least some wolves start with the [[Bite]] special ability when tamed as [[hunter]] [[pet]]s.
* Wolves are [[skinnable]].

=== Examples ===
* Snow Tracker Wolf ([[Dun Morogh]])
* Plains Tracker ([[Mulgore]])
* [[Coyote]] ([[Westfall]])

== [[Ghost Wolf]] ==
[[Shaman]] of moderate ability can change their form into a [[Ghost Wolf]]. This allows them to travel much faster than an average humanoid, but this ritual only works outdoors.

== As A [[Hunter]] Pet ==
* Has medium damage, medium armor, and medium HP.
* Eats only Meat.
* Can learn [[Growl]], [[Cower]], [[Dash]], [[Bite]], and their own skill, [[Furious Howl]].
* The Mist Howler, Prairie Wolf Alpha, Deathmaw, Slavering Worg, Bloodaxe Worg, and Mist Howler are relatively popular for their faster swing speeds.  
* A popular pet, due to a variety of colors, some wolves with fast swing speed, Furious Howl, and Dash.
* Worgs, when tamed as a hunter pet, are in the same category as wolves and have the same skills.

[[image:wildkin.png|thumb|]]

The Wildkin have long been considered a sacred animal by the [[Night Elves]], and the [[Tauren]].  The Priests of [[Elune]] see the Wildkin as embued with the spirit and strength of the Moon Goddess, and the druids see them as guardians and protectors of nature.  Night Elf legends hold that the Wildkin were created by Elune in the distant past to guard her sacred shrines and glades with he strength of a bear abd the intelligent of an owl.  Many believe there is a great deal of truth to this myth, as Wildkin tend to congregate around ancient places of power.  Over time however, many Wildkin seem to have either forgotten their sacred charge, or lost the site they were trying to guard and now roam across both continents.  Wildkin tend to be fiercly territorial and will attack anyone they meet.  They resemble a cross between an Owl and a Bear, hence their more common name, Owlbears.  They stand upright at about 10 to 12 feet tall, and their body is covered in hairy feathers, usually brown or white.  Their arms have a wing like shape that end in clawed talons, and their heads have a beak and horns.  These odd creatures also emit a distinctive sound when riled, sounding like a combination of growl and screech.  Wildkin feathers are very highly prized in certain circles for their rare magical properties.

Also known as:
*Owlbeast
*Owlbear

Clan of [[Forest Trolls]] located in the [[Arathi Highlands]], and [[Hinterlands]]. The clan is at war with the [[Wildhammer Clan]] of [[Aerie Peak]] The tribe is part of the Zul-Amani Empire.

The [[Stormwind]] '''Wizard's Sanctum''' is the mystic pocket plane in which the [[Alliance]]'s sorcerers and battlemages research, train and experiment. After the fall of Dalaran, many young wizards and mages relocated to Stormwind's Mage Quarter, where bountiful ley energies still lay untained by the Burning Legion. Led by [[Maginor Dumas]], the magi strive to decipher arcane mysteries and uncover eldritch lore. [[Larimaine Purdue]], the resident portalmancer, has created a rift portal deep in the Sanctum, but she keeps under close guard and will for now not let anyone venture through its swirling vortex.

The Sancum is more officially called the Academy of the Arcane Sciences, and it is the foremost center of arcane research and study today. Many High Elves also seek refuse in the arcane halls, quenching their addiction and thrist to power in a safer environment.

===Getting Faction===

[[Rivern Frostwind]] offers three quests. You gain fifty Reputations Points for each turn-in so you must do the quests a total of 840 times to get the [[mount]].

The first quest, [[Frostsaber Provisions]] [http://wow.allakhazam.com/db/quest.html?wquest=4970 (Allakhazam)], is avalaible at level 58. It requires five [[Shardtooth Meat]] from the [[Elder Shardtooths]] [http://wow.allakhazam.com/db/mob.html?wmob=7445 (Allakhazam)] and five [[Chillwind Meat]] from the [[Chillwind Ravagers]] [http://wow.allakhazam.com/db/mob.html?wmob=7449 (Allakhazam)].

The second quest, [[Winterfall Intrusion]] [http://wow.allakhazam.com/db/quest.html?wquest=5201 (Allakhazam)], is avaliable after gaining 1500 Points (halfway to friendly). You need to kill five [[Winterfall Shamans]] [http://wow.allakhazam.com/db/mob.html?wmob=7439 (Allakhazam)] and five [[Winterfall Ursas]] [http://wow.allakhazam.com/db/mob.html?wmob=7438 (Allakhazam)] located in [[Winterfall Village]], east of [[Everlook]]. This will also give reputation points for [[Timbermaw Furbolgs]] faction.

The third quest, [[Rampaging Giants]] [http://wow.allakhazam.com/db/quest.html?wquest=5981 (Allakhazam)], is an elite quest and is avaliable when you get [[Honored]]. You need to kill four [[Frostmaul Giants]] [http://wow.allakhazam.com/db/mob.html?wmob=7428 (Allakhazam)] and four [[Frostmaul Preservers]] [http://wow.allakhazam.com/db/mob.html?wmob=7429 (Allakhazam)] located in [[Dark Whispergorge]] in southern [[Winterspring]].

The naga presence in Nendis has been broken, and their commanders lie dead. For the first time since Illidan’s invasion, the ruins may finally be free of their grasp. Still, this victory belongs not only to my sentinels.

The High Priestess must be informed.

Tyrande Whisperwind watches over all our people, and she should know what has been accomplished here. The fall of Illidan’s lieutenants is no small matter.Travel to her and deliver this news.

Tell her the Tideblade are broken, and that Narvalis Point still stands vigilant.

Lady Serpentia and Ta'jax are dead?

Those names were spoken often during the war against Illidan. Their warbands left scars along this coast that have not yet faded. If they have truly fallen, then one of the last shadows from that time has finally been lifted.

Nendis has been silent for far too long. With the naga driven out, the ruins may finally be reclaimed. Not quickly. Wounds like these take time to heal. But in time… our people will return. Homes will be rebuilt. Temples restored. The forests will hear our voices again.

Moonwhisper Coast was once a place where the kaldorei lived in peace beneath Elune's light. Perhaps, slowly, it may become so again.

You have helped make that future possible, <class>. Know that the sentinels of Narvalis Point have my gratitude… and so do you.
